name: Clean checkpoint: five forecasting methods x two decision methods at two origins
question: Which forecasting method, combined with which decision method, gives the cheapest realised bed-capacity plan, and how much does it improve on simple baselines and on simply following the forecast?

data.blanks: months with a blank value are dropped
data.cutoff_rule: rows after a cut-off are discarded before any value is converted

forecasts.common: each method forecasts occupied and available separately, six months ahead, from the 24-month training window only
forecasts.Persistence: last month of the window, flat
forecasts.Seasonal naive: same calendar month one year earlier

SARIMA-24.target_scaling: StandardScaler fitted on the 24 window values; forecasts inverse-transformed

ExtraTrees-24.feature_rule: lags and shifted rolling mean/std (ddof 1) of the target, plus calendar values
ExtraTrees-24.training_rows: rows whose features need data before the window are dropped (12 rows expected)
ExtraTrees-24.forecasting: recursive, six steps, earlier predictions feed later features
ExtraTrees-24.note: the project pipeline's median imputer is a no-op here because no feature is missing

decisions.Rule: x_t = max(0, forecast gap), clipped in month order to 0 <= x_t <= 15,000 and the ramp limits (if a ramp binds, move as far toward the forecast gap as allowed); a_t, r_t follow from changes in x_t
decisions.LP: minimise sum_t (500 x_t + 550 a_t + 300 r_t + 5000 s_t) s.t. x_t + s_t - u_t = forecast gap_t; x_t = x_{t-1} + a_t - r_t; x_0 = 0; 0 <= x_t <= 15,000; 0 <= a_t, r_t <= 5,000; s_t, u_t >= 0; continuous; no terminal charge; solver PuLP CBC, one thread
decisions.Hindsight: the LP solved with the actual gaps

scoring: each plan is held fixed; realised cost = sum_t (500 x_t + 550 a_t + 300 r_t) + 5000 sum_t max(0, d_t - x_t) with actual gaps; no shortfall deadband; a_t and r_t are the positive and negative parts of x_t - x_{t-1}

per_origin: tie band for cost: 1% of that origin's hindsight cost
tie band for gap MAE: 5 beds
rank the 10 plans by realised cost; plans within the tie band of the cheapest are 'joint best'
across_origins: overall cost ranking: by combined excess over hindsight (sum over the two origins of plan cost minus that origin's hindsight cost)

'clear winner': a plan that is joint best at both origins, or that beats the overall runner-up by more than the tie band at each origin; otherwise report 'no clear winner' and list the joint-best plans
best forecast: lowest mean gap MAE across both origins; 'clear' only if lowest at both origins by more than 5 beds
improvement_measures: value of optimisation: Rule cost - LP cost for each method
saving vs Persistence and vs Seasonal naive: baseline cost - plan cost (the same decision method for both)
share of avoidable cost removed: (baseline cost - plan cost) / (baseline cost - hindsight cost), as a percentage, for baselines Persistence LP and Seasonal naive LP
forecast skill vs Seasonal naive: 1 - (method MAE / Seasonal naive MAE), for the gap, occupied and available
excess over hindsight, in model units and as a percentage of hindsight cost
all reported per origin and combined
literal_readings: if more than one plan meets the 'clear winner' definition, every such plan is reported as a joint winner and none is singled out
'runner-up' is the second plan in the overall ranking; exact ties in combined excess keep the fixed plan order
'lowest at both origins by more than 5 beds' means lower than every other method by more than 5 beds at each origin

combined ratios are ratios of sums: share = (sum baseline - sum plan) / (sum baseline - sum hindsight); skill = 1 - mean MAE of the method / mean MAE of Seasonal naive; excess % = sum of excess / sum of hindsight cost
ranks use realised cost; plans with identical cost share a rank

disclosures: Oct 2025 - Sep 2026 actuals were used in earlier, separate tests; the rules are fixed before this run but are not blind
NHS revised Sep 2026 between the September and October 2026 publications (available -87, occupied -2)
the October 2026 publication is used throughout
SARIMA-24 uses all 24 months as labels; the project's original procedure dropped 12 and required at least 30
ExtraTrees-24 uses settings selected for occupied beds on available beds too, and has about 12 training rows
costs are illustrative model units (validated: False)
procedure: write and hash this config before any forecast
plan stage: forecasts and plans for both origins from data up to each cut-off; hash them
score stage: verify both hashes, load outcomes, solve hindsight, score once, apply the rules
